page.layout: Running head at top: "HEXILOGIÆ CAP. XIII." with page number "580" at top left. One text column in the centre, set in italic. Marginal notes in the left margin, beside the lines of the text. Catchword at lower right.

l.i: institutionem, ad rem domesticam gubernandam
adq; publicam necessaria. Succedunt tandem his fa-
cultates (ut appellantur) summa, hominemq; bene
informatum & instructum in suo genere ad πρακτικὴν[?]
velut ducentes manu, θεολογικὴν, νομικὴν, ἰατρικὴν.
Quarum illa quae Theologia appellatur, fontes suos
non alibi quam in coelo habet, rivi in homines verbo
& scriptura Dei ex mera ejusdem gratia defluxe-
runt: haec vero fontes suos ab orbis conditu in philoso-
phiae penetralibus, naturae ipsa duce & teste habue-
runt. Ethicam enim jurisprudentia, Physicam Me-
dicina quam latissime ad commoditatem generis
hu-mani privatim & publice deduxerunt.Gymnasiorum
igitur species quatuor ex hoc ordine (nam tot fuerunt
olim) constitui possunt. Prima eorum, in quibus lin-
guarum doctrina exponitur; secunda, in quibus in-
strumenta subministrantur & artes ad philosophiam
prævia: tertia, in quibus aperiuntur studiosis & pa-
tescunt recessus philosophiae: quarta denique eorum,
in quibus summa illa facultates juventuti explanan-
tur ex usu Reipub. Ex his patet, quisnam sit doctrina
ordo in tradendis disciplinis. Rem totam paucis con-
clusionibus complectemur. Plura sunt apud Boëti-
um, qui scripsit de ordine tradendi disciplin. in
lib. de doctrina scholarium, & Plutarchum in
lib. de contrarietatibus Stoicorum, & Philo-
nem Judæum in libr. de agricultura, Augusti-
num lib. de ordine & deniq; Conimbricenses
in procem. phys. q. 5. Prima conclusio sit:
Veteres Græci non necesse habebant discere Grammati-
cam. Nam illorum lingua in scholasteriis
personabat. Hodie res aliter se habet.

marginalia.note: Grammatica doctrinae ordine est prior Logica.

page.notes: Greek word after "ad" (πρακτικὴν) is doubtful, accents not clear at this scan resolution. The ligature "æ" in "prævia" and the "Judæum" are read as printed but uncertain. Whether the body text is entirely italic or some Latin references (e.g. "lib. de doctrina scholarium") are roman could not be fully separated; the roman/italic split of the references is approximate. Printed s forms (shown as f in the scan, e.g. "tefcunt", "phyf.q.5") were normalised to plain s per the long-s rule. "deniq;" and "adq;" are copied as printed. The marginal notes "I." to "IV." are read as the numbered list beside the text lines. The page number and running head are copied from the print.
